title: SSRF guard bypass: redirect TOCTOU, DNS rebind, absolute-URL injection, parser confusion
index_line: T-0003 · NET_CONNECT · the guard validates one interpretation, the client acts on another · corroborated
invariant_violated: The SSRF guard validates one interpretation of the URL (first hop, first resolution, parsed path) while the HTTP client acts on another.

mechanism.does: attacker controls a URL the server will fetch (webhook/avatar/import/preview/baseURL override)
guard parses and checks: allowlist, isPrivateIP, scheme filter
guard decision made on the initial interpretation
bypass: redirect followed without per-hop revalidation, DNS rebind at connect time, absolute-URL escape from baseURL, or parser confusion (userinfo/backslash/bracket/alt-IP)
client connects to internal service, metadata IP, or attacker host
impact: response content (metadata creds, internal data) or the forwarded Authorization header reaches the attacker

sink.http.request.value: server-side fetch of the user-influenced URL

guard.ssrf.value: the guard and its bypass class: redirect-policy | resolve-pinning | absolute-URL | parser-confusion

header.forwarding.value: does Authorization/bearer follow the cross-origin request? (credential leak flavor)

preconditions.expr: a guard exists in front of the fetch (else it is plain SSRF, not this record)
user input reaches the fetch URL
varies — webhook/import features usually authenticated user

success: request observed at a canary host (OAST or controlled listener)
Authorization/bearer header seen at the canary — credential leak variant
metadata (169.254.169.254) or internal service content returned
redirect to internal target followed with no per-hop revalidation
failure_like: redirect target re-validated per hop — blocked
DNS resolution pinned at the guard — rebind fails
false_positive: client correctly strips Authorization on cross-origin redirects (not a finding)
guard re-checks and pins — record verdict and move on

hazards: guard primitives differ per runtime (isPrivateIP vs url.Parse vs InetAddress.isSiteLocalAddress) — test the pair, not one side
cloud metadata ranges differ (169.254.169.254 vs metadata.google.internal)
non_transfers: no outbound fetch in the app
